Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: 1-week history of sore throat progressing to dry, non-productive cough; exertional shortness of breath with mild wheeze and chest discomfort; intermittent headaches; subjective low-grade fever (resolved); reduced appetite without weight loss.  
- Relevant family medical history: Mother had lung cancer; no known family history of thromboembolic disease.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): None reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Performs walking and exercise “now and then”; currently experiencing reduced appetite; no weight change reported.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Non-smoker (tried “once or twice”); no alcohol or other substance use discussed.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Expressed health anxiety regarding serious illnesses; no formal mood assessment recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives and works in the UK; required 2 days sick leave this week; no other social details recorded.  

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not performed.  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute upper-airway illness with sore throat → dry cough; exertional SOB/wheeze; afebrile now; overall mild course and beginning to improve; no alarming weight loss, haemoptysis, or high-risk exposures.  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
• Acute viral upper respiratory infection / viral bronchitis – most likely given typical timeline and improving trend.  
• COVID-19 infection – moderate likelihood; symptom cluster fits, though no anosmia or test performed.  
• Reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma – possible; wheeze and exertional SOB could represent first episode triggered by recent viral infection.

Working diagnosis: Probable acute viral URTI/viral bronchitis; monitor for deterioration or evolving features of COVID-19 or asthma.  

Management priorities: Provide symptomatic relief, certify sick leave, safety-net advice to seek face-to-face review if worsening or no improvement in 4–5 days; consider COVID testing and in-person exam if symptoms persist or escalate.  

Management Plan

- Symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), adequate oral fluids, rest.  
- Issued sick note for a few additional days off work.  
- Safety-net: advised to seek GP/urgent review if breathlessness increases, sudden change occurs, or symptoms fail to improve within 4–5 days.  
- No medications prescribed beyond simple analgesia.  
- No immediate investigations ordered; advised COVID test if accessible (not explicitly stated but implied by concern).  
- Follow-up: Patient to re-contact medical services if not improving or if concerned.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / viral bronchitis – High likelihood: classic sore throat → dry cough course, mild fever, gradual improvement.  
2. COVID-19 infection – Moderate likelihood: overlapping symptom constellation with fluctuating course.  
3. Reactive airway disease / new-onset asthma – Moderate likelihood: wheeze and exertional SOB without prior asthma history, possibly virus-triggered.

Quality checks

● Missing but expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse, temperature), height/weight/BMI, urinalysis, immunisation review, alcohol intake details, formal mental health screening, vision and hearing screening, preventive health status (flu/Pap/colorectal checks).  
● Internal contradictions: Transcript lists date of birth “09/05/2016” yet patient discusses adult work life—conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional overlaps and minor audio gaps but clinical information understandable.
